video_title: Isiah Thomas, Tim Hardaway Sr. & Lindsey Hunter Tell Untold NBA Stories 👀 | The Crossover Podcast

quotes.speaker: Tim Hardaway Sr.
quotes.summary_phrase: Tim Hardaway Sr. on coaches failing to challenge players
quotes.excerpt: they don't like to get in the player's face. They don't want no confrontation.
quotes.quote: It is a lot of things, but they don't like to get in the player's face. They don't want no confrontation. They don't want to talk to them because they think the players will get bent out of shape. You don't go to the rim or take the basketball to the basket in the third quarter, and something is a problem, and you don't tell them that? That is a problem. To me, that is a problem. I mean, what are your assistant coaches doing? I mean, they are just collecting a check. That is what I am saying. Look, we have to go to the basket. That is what happened with Houston, and that is what Chris Paul was telling James Harden. We haven't went to the basket not one time. We settled for shooting threes, and they kept shooting threes. That is why they lost.

quotes.speaker: Lindsey Hunter
quotes.summary_phrase: Lindsey Hunter on Mark Price's dominance during his rookie year
quotes.excerpt: Mark Price is having his way with me. I mean, he is killing me.

text_blocks.text: I never forget we were playing Cleveland, and Mark Price is having his way with me. I mean, he is killing me. Coming off screens, wow, wow, wow. They call timeout, I come to the bench, Chuck Daly says, Lindsey, Mark Price is killing you. Killing you.

text_blocks.speaker: Lindsey Hunter
text_blocks.text: Everybody on me. Zeke, what you going to do? Benny would have the towel, Zeke, what, hey man, Mark Price is killing you. He is killing you. I am like, all right, okay, okay, okay. Go back out again, do his thing, Mark Price, wow, wow, wow, wow, wow. Timeout. Isaiah, he is killing you.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim Hardaway Sr.
text_blocks.text: I know he killing you, Zeke.

text_blocks.speaker: Lindsey Hunter
text_blocks.text: I say, hey look, I know he is killing me. He is 20,000 people in here, know he is killing me. Everybody watching on television know he is killing me. Can you tell me something that is going to help me stop this dude from killing me? Because if you can't tell me that, don't talk to me. I don't want to hear it.

quotes.speaker: Tim Hardaway Sr.
quotes.summary_phrase: Tim Hardaway Sr. on the difficulty of guarding quick players
quotes.excerpt: I never played against a white guy that was that quick. That fast with the basketball.
quotes.quote: I never played against a white guy that was that quick. That fast with the basketball. Man, and stop on a dime. I mean, stop. And pull up. He did beat me. I played one, the first very first game, I played against him. Don Nelson called a timeout. He is saying the same thing to you, Tim. He is killing you. My rookie year, I was like, wow. When you see it on TV and then you play against him, it is different. It is different. I mean, he comes down, he splits the pick and roll, and he gets through that double team so quick and splits it. He be like, on a dime. How did he get through that?

quotes.summary_phrase: Isiah Thomas on the philosophical challenge of Jordan's legacy

quotes.quote: Belief is a powerful message in terms of what you believe. If you believe it, then you feel it. And the believability about some of the things aren't true. Even if you even though you believe it, you have a hard time in your mind understanding and seeing truth. Because when truth is presented in front of you and it is facts, your belief system overrides the truth. And we see that daily, not only in sport but also in life. So that is the philosophical standpoint. So when you talk about philosophers like Kant, Hegel, you know, those two in particular, right? If you want to philosophize, read up on those two and and see what they their thoughts around belief, honesty, hospitality.
